note: Authored pack: s24 (APIs/FastAPI) theory+interview+coding, s25 (Analytics) logic+debug, s26 (MLOps/Docker/AWS) solved+defense+checkpoint — 20 each.

items.q: REST ke core constraints kya hain (interview me 3 bolo)?
items.a: Statelessness (har request me poora context), uniform interface (resources + standard methods), aur client-server separation. Iske alawa cacheability aur layered system production APIs me practically zaroori hain.

items.q: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE — kaunsa idempotent hai aur kaunsa nahi?
items.a: GET, PUT, DELETE idempotent hain (same request dobara chalane se state same rehta hai); POST idempotent nahi hota (naya record ban sakta hai); PATCH implementation par depend karta hai.

items.q: HTTP status codes ke families ka matlab batao (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx).
items.a: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (request galat — 400 validation, 401 auth, 403 permission, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 429 rate limit), 5xx server error (500 bug, 503 unavailable).

items.q: FastAPI me request validation kaise hoti hai?
items.a: Pydantic models type hints se schema banate hain; incoming body/query/path validate hote hain aur invalid input par automatic 422 with field-level errors milta hai. Isliye validation code manual likhne ki zarurat nahi.

items.q: Async endpoints kab fayde dete hain aur kab nahi?
items.a: Jab endpoint I/O-bound ho (DB, HTTP calls) aur awaitable client use ho — tab concurrency milti hai. Agar andar blocking library call hai (time.sleep, sync DB driver) to async fayda khatam aur loop block hota hai.

items.q: Dependency injection FastAPI me kya solve karta hai?
items.a: Reusable dependencies (auth, DB session, config, rate limit) ko declare karke per-request inject karta hai — testing me overrides se fake pass kar sakte ho, aur clean-up (finally) automatic hoti hai.

items.q: API authentication ke common options aur trade-off likho.
items.a: API key (simple, static, rotation zaroori), JWT (stateless, par revoke mushkil aur short TTL + refresh chahiye), session cookie (server state, browser flows ke liye), OAuth2 (third-party delegation). Secret ko env se lo, code me nahi.

items.q: Rate limiting ke algorithms aur header ka role batao.
items.a: Token bucket/bucket window (burst allow), fixed window (simple par boundary spike), sliding log (precise par memory). Response me X-RateLimit-Remaining/Retry-After bhejo taaki client backoff kar sake.
items.x: Limits + headers, warna client guess karega.

items.q: Pagination ke do patterns aur unka trade-off batao.
items.a: Offset/limit simple hai par bade offset par slow aur insertion se skip/duplicate. Keyset/cursor stable aur fast hai (index-friendly), par random page access nahi. Large datasets me cursor.

items.q: Idempotency key kaise implement karte ho?
items.a: Client Idempotency-Key header bhejta hai; server key ko store karke result cache karta hai aur same key par wahi response deta hai (different body ke saath 409). POST create endpoints ke liye standard practice.

items.q: API versioning ke approach aur recommendation batao.
items.a: URL versioning (/v1/) sabse visible aur cache-friendly; header versioning URL clean rakhta hai par debug mushkil. Breaking changes ke liye naya version, additive changes ke liye same version + deprecation window.

items.q: Global error handling ka structure kya hona chahiye?
items.a: Ek exception handler jo domain errors ko status + stable error code + human message me map kare, unexpected errors par 500 with trace id (details logs me, response me nahi). Error response ka shape sab endpoints me same rakho.

items.q: Structured logging me kya-kya field hote hain?
items.a: timestamp, level, request id/correlation id, route, method, status, latency, user/tenant (masked), aur error type. JSON logs machine-parseable hote hain — print statements production me nahi.

items.q: Health check aur readiness probe me farq?
items.a: Liveness health check batata hai process zinda hai (restart trigger), readiness batata hai dependencies (DB/cache) ke saath serve karne layak hai (traffic start). Dono separate rakho, warna DB down par pod restart loop ho jaata hai.

items.q: Config 12-factor style kaise rakhte ho?
items.a: Config env vars se (defaults code me), startup par validate (fail fast), secrets env/secret manager se, aur code repo me sirf .env.example placeholders. Environment-specific branches code me nahi hone chahiye.
items.x: Config env se, code se nahi.

items.q: CORS kab lagta hai aur galat config ka symptom kya hai?
items.a: Browser jab different origin se API call karta hai to preflight (OPTIONS) + Access-Control-Allow-Origin chahiye. Galat allowed origins se browser me CORS error aata hai (server logs me request aa jaati hai) — curl kaam karta hai, browser nahi.
items.x: Browser ka restriction, server ka nahi.

items.q: OpenAPI/Swagger spec ka production fayda kya hai (sirf docs nahi)?
items.a: Contract-generated clients, request/response validation in tests, breaking-change detection (schema diff), aur gateway/monitoring tooling integrations — isliye spec ko source of truth maano.

items.q: API testing ke layers likho (unit → integration → contract).
items.a: Unit: pure functions/Jawab logic. Integration: real app + test client + test DB (validation, status codes, auth). Contract: spec vs responses (schema assertions). Plus ek smoke test deploy ke baad.

items.q: Deployment me workers aur concurrency ka relation kya hai (uvicorn/gunicorn)?
items.a: CPU-bound kaam par multiple worker processes, I/O-bound async code par chhoti worker count + high concurrency. Rule: workers ≈ CPU cores (ya 2×CPU+1 classic), aur memory/tail latency measure karke tune.

items.q: Downstream API ke liye timeout, retry aur circuit breaker kaise combine karoge?
items.a: Har call par strict timeout (connect + read), bounded retries with backoff+jitter sirf safe/idempotent methods par, aur circuit breaker jo failure threshold par fast-fail kare. Fallback/cache response do, warna upstream issue tumhara outage ban jaata hai.

items.q: Interview: 'Ek endpoint design karo jo order create kare' — kya-kya bataoge?
items.a: POST /v1/orders with JSON body, Pydantic validation, auth (JWT), idempotency key header, transactional insert, 201 + Location, 400 validation, 409 conflict, 422 semantic error, aur structured logs with trace id. Rate limiting + audit log bhi mention karo.

items.q: Interview: '401 aur 403 me farq batao, aur 404 kab 403 ki jagah dete ho?'
items.a: 401 = authenticate nahi hua (credential missing/invalid), 403 = authenticated par permission nahi. Security-sensitive resources me unauthorized user ko 404 dete hain taaki existence leak na ho.

items.q: Interview: 'API ko 1000 req/s par kaise la jaoge?'
items.a: Measure karo pehle (p95, DB time). Phir: async workers + pool sizing, DB indexes + query shape, caching (response/Redis), pagination limits, gateway rate limits, aur horizontal scale with stateless design. Bottleneck har layer par alag hai.

items.q: Interview: 'N+1 problem API me kaise dikhta hai?'
items.a: List endpoint har item ke liye extra query karta hai (ORM lazy loading) — response slow, DB load high. Fix: eager loading/join, batch fetch, ya dataloader pattern; log query count per request aur test me assert karo.

items.q: Interview: 'Breaking change safely kaise deploy karoge?'
items.a: Expand-contract: naya field optional add karo, clients migrate karao (versioned), purana field deprecate with sunset header/date, metrics se usage verify karo, phir remove. Big-bang rename kabhi nahi.

items.q: Interview: 'API ka secret rotation kaise karoge?'
items.a: Dual-key support (old + new valid), new key issue karo, clients ko overlap window me migrate karao, usage metrics se old key ka traffic 0 verify karo, phir old key revoke. Downtime zero.

items.q: Interview: 'Request body size limits kyun zaroori hain?'
items.a: Warna memory exhaustion/DoS possible hai. Gateway + app level limit (jaise 1MB JSON), file uploads alag endpoint par streaming ke saath, aur 413 status. Limit exceed par clear error do.

items.q: Interview: 'Timeouts client aur server dono side kyun hone chahiye?'
items.a: Client timeout ke bina thread/connection hang rehta hai; server timeout ke bina slow downstream workers kha jaata hai. Dono + retry budget (total deadline) define karo, warna retries stack hokar storm bana dete hain.

items.q: Webhook endpoint likho jo HMAC signature verify kare aur event id se duplicate delivery dedupe kare.
Interview: 'PATCH vs PUT me production concern kya hai?'
items.a: PUT poora resource replace karta hai (missing fields null/default ho sakte hain), PATCH partial update karta hai. PATCH me concurrency ke liye If-Match/version use karo warna last-write-wins data loss dega.

items.q: Interview: 'API pagination me total count dena chahiye ya nahi?'
items.a: Agar count sasta hai (cached/estimated) to do; warna expensive COUNT(*) se p95 kharab hota hai. Practical: cursor ke saath has_more do, aur exact total ko alag endpoint/async job me rakho.

items.q: Interview: 'API downtime ke doraan graceful degradation kaise karoge?'
items.a: Critical paths (auth, checkout) ko prioirty, non-critical (recommendations, analytics) off karo; cache/stale-while-revalidate se serve karo; maintenance mode with 503 + Retry-After; aur feature flags se quickly disable.

items.q: Interview: 'File upload endpoint design karo.'
items.a: Streaming upload (multipart), size + content-type validation, virus/zip-bomb protection, temporary storage → background processing, pre-signed URL pattern for large files, aur progress/status endpoint. Memory me poori file na load karo.

items.q: Interview: 'Test client se API kaise test karoge?'
items.a: FastAPI TestClient/httpx se app invoke karo with overridden dependencies (test DB), assert status + body schema + side effects, aur failure cases (invalid input, unauthorized, conflict) bhi cover karo.

items.q: Interview: 'Production me 500 errors spike — pehle 5 minute me kya karoge?'
items.a: Rollback/flag off agar recent deploy se correlate karein, error rate + trace samples dekho, saturation (CPU/mem/DB pool) check karo, aur status page update. Root cause baad me — pehle impact kam karo.

items.q: Interview: 'CORS issue production me debug karo.'
items.a: Browser devtools me exact preflight/response headers dekho, allowed origin exact match (wildcard with credentials invalid hai), OPTIONS route allow karo, aur Vary: Origin. Server logs me request aa rahi hai to issue browser-side hai.

items.q: Interview: 'API ke liye caching strategy batao.'
items.a: GET par ETag/Last-Modified + 304 (browser/CDN), response cache (Redis) with short TTL for expensive reads, aur cache key me user/tenant scope. Writes par explicit invalidation karo.

items.q: Interview: 'Observability ke teen pillars API me kaise lagate ho?'
items.a: Metrics (latency percentiles, error rate, saturation), logs (structured with request id), aur traces (spans per downstream call) — teeno me same request id se correlate karo.

items.q: Interview: 'API security checklist (5 points) batao.'
items.a: Authn/authz per endpoint, input validation + size limits, parameterized queries, secrets in env/manager, rate limits + audit logs; plus HTTPS only and security headers.

items.q: Load test harness likho jo concurrent requests bhejkar p50/p95 latency aur error rate report kare.
Interview: 'API me background jobs kaise handle karoge?'
items.a: Request me job enqueue karo (queue/Redis), 202 + job id return, worker process job chalaye with retries + idempotency, aur status endpoint se polling. Sync me lamba kaam mat karo — timeout ho jaata hai.

items.q: Interview: 'Multi-tenant API me data isolation kaise ensure karoge?'
items.a: Tenant id ko auth token se derive karo (client input se nahi), har query me mandatory tenant filter (row-level security ya ORM default scope), aur tests jo cross-tenant access fail karte hain.
items.x: Tenant auth se, query me enforce.

items.q: FastAPI me Pydantic model ke saath typed endpoint likho (validation + status code).
items.x: Field constraints se validation automatic hai.

items.q: FastAPI dependency se auth aur current user inject karo.
Consistent error handler likho (domain error → status + code).
Cursor-based pagination ka helper likho (keyset).
items.x: limit+1 se has_more pata chalta hai.

items.q: Rate limiting dependency likho (in-memory token bucket).
items.a:
import time
from collections import defaultdict

_buckets = defaultdict(lambda: [10.0, time.time()])

def rate_limit(key: str, rate=10.0, per=1.0):
    tokens, last = _buckets[key]
    now = time.time()
    tokens = min(rate, tokens + (now - last) * rate / per)
    if tokens < 1:
        _buckets[key] = [tokens, now]
        raise DomainError('rate limit exceeded')
    _buckets[key] = [tokens - 1, now]
items.x: Production me Redis/shared store use karo.

items.q: Idempotency key support likho (store me result cache).
items.a:
def create_with_idempotency(store, key, payload, create_fn):
    if key in store:
        return store[key], False
    result = create_fn(payload)
    store[key] = result
    return result, True

# controller: result, created = create_with_idempotency(STORE, key, payload, do_create)
# return 201 if created else 200 (same body)
items.x: Same key = same body, duplicate nahi.

items.q: Request logging middleware likho (latency + request id).
items.a:
import time, uuid
from fastapi import Request

@app.middleware('http')
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    rid = request.headers.get('x-request-id', str(uuid.uuid4()))
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000
    response.headers['x-request-id'] = rid
    print(f'{rid} {request.method} {request.url.path} {response.status_code} {ms:.1f}ms')
    return response
items.x: Request id client tak return karo — support easy.

items.q: Health aur readiness endpoints likho (alag semantics).
items.x: Liveness sasta, readiness dependency check kare.

items.q: Downstream HTTP call ko timeout + retry ke saath wrap karo.
Config ko env se load karke startup par validate karo.
items.x: Startup par fail karo, runtime par nahi.

items.q: Tenant-scoped query likho jahan tenant auth se aata hai.
items.x: Tenant filter mandatory, auth se derive.

items.q: API response caching with ETag likho.
items.x: 304 se bandwidth aur latency bachti hai.

items.q: Pydantic response model se output filter karo (sensitive fields leak na hon).
Background task pattern likho (202 + job id).
items.x: Production me durable queue (Redis/RQ/Celery) use karo.

items.q: API ke liye integration test likho (validation + status codes).
items.a:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_create_order():
    ok = client.post('/v1/orders', json={'item': 'book', 'qty': 2})
    assert ok.status_code == 201
    bad = client.post('/v1/orders', json={'item': '', 'qty': 0})
    assert bad.status_code == 422
    assert 'detail' in bad.json()
items.x: Happy path + validation path dono test karo.

items.q: Graceful shutdown par in-flight requests aur resources handle karo.
items.a:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.pool = create_pool()      # startup
    yield
    app.state.pool.close()              # shutdown: connections clean

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
items.x: Lifespan se pool leak nahi hota.

items.q: OpenAPI schema generate karke contract test karo.
items.a:
import json
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_openapi_contract():
    spec = client.get('/openapi.json').json()
    paths = spec['paths']
    assert '/v1/orders' in paths
    assert 'post' in paths['/v1/orders']
    body = paths['/v1/orders']['post']['requestBody']['content']['application/json']['schema']
    assert body['$ref'].endswith('Order')
items.x: Schema assert karo — drift pakdi jaayegi.

items.q: Query params ko validate karo (limit bounds + sorting whitelist).
items.x: Whitelist = SQL injection aur nonsense se bachav.

items.q: BI report me 'total sales' ka sum rows ke average se match nahi kar raha. Kaunsi concept chal rahi hai?
items.a: Filter context: tabular visual ka row-level context aggregate ko change karta hai, jabki card/overall visual poore context par aggregate karta hai. KPI ko denominator/context ke saath define karo, warna same naam ke do numbers aayenge.
items.x: Context aggregate ka matlab badalta hai.

items.q: Ratio metric (conversion rate) ko sum karne par galat aata hai — kyun?
items.a: Ratios additive nahi hote; Σ(num)/Σ(den) karo, average of ratios nahi. Power BI/Excel me measure = DIVIDE(SUM(conv), SUM(visits)), aur zero denominator par DIVIDE/IFERROR se bachao.

items.q: Star schema me fact aur dimension table ka farq operational terms me batao.
items.a: Fact table events/measures rakhti hai (orders, revenue) aur dimensions attributes (customer, product, date). Isi split se slicing/filtering fast hoti hai aur DAX measures simple rehte hain.
items.x: Measures fact me, attributes dimension me.

items.q: Relationship cardinality many-to-many ho to kya problem aati hai?
items.a: Ambiguous aggregation (numbers duplicate ya under-count ho jaate hain) aur slow queries. Fix: bridge table banao (grain define karke) ya grain ko fact me le aao, phir tests se expected totals verify karo.

items.q: Time intelligence me YTD calculate karne ka sahi basis kya hai?
items.a: Ek proper date dimension (continuous dates, marked as date table) chahiye; uske bina TOTALYTD/DATESYTD unreliable hote hain. Fiscal year ho to fiscal calendar mapping dimension me rakho.
items.x: Date dimension ke bina time intelligence nahi.

items.q: KPI me 'active user' define karne ke do options aur farq?
items.a: Options: unique users with any event in period vs users crossing an engagement threshold (n events in 7 days). Pehla sasta par inflated, doosra meaningful par complex. Definition document karo aur ek hi use karo.

items.q: Report refresh ke baad numbers badal gaye (kal vs aaj). Kaunsi cheezein check karoge?
items.a: Data snapshot/late-arriving data, time zone/day boundary, source system change, aur report filter context. Isliye 'as of' timestamp display karo aur daily snapshot table rakho taaki history stable rahe.
items.x: Snapshot ke bina history badalti rehti hai.

items.q: Seasonality ko moving average se kaise dekhoge?
items.a: Rolling 7/28-day average se weekly seasonality smooth hoti hai aur trend dikhta hai; year-over-year comparison se seasonality compare hoti hai. Raw daily numbers se trend claim mat karo.

items.q: Top-N visual me 'Others' category kyun zaroori hai?
items.a: Warna long tail ka total gayab ho jaata hai aur percentages 100% se match nahi karte. Practical: top 10 + Others, aur 'Others' ko aggregate karne ke baad hi share calculate karo.

items.q: Cumulative (running total) visual me gaps kyun aate hain?
items.a: Days jahan data nahi hai woh date dimension me nahi hote, isliye cumulative line me jump theek but gaps dikhte hain. Fix: date dimension se join karo aur CALCULATE ke saath ALLSELECTED/ALL use karo.

items.q: Drill-down me numbers change ho jaate hain. Kaunsi inconsistency?
items.a: Different levels par different aggregation (parent me distinct customers, child me counts) ho rahi hai. Har level ka metric explicitly define karo aur totals ko non-additive mark karo.

items.q: Report me 'no data' rows dikhane ke liye kya karte ho?
items.a: Date/category dimension ke saath POISSON/blank-fill join karo (ya crossjoin) aur count 0 dikhao — warna trend me din gayab ho jaate hain. Saath me 'days with no data' count report karo.

items.q: Slicer aur page-level filter ka interaction samjhao.
items.a: Filters intersect karte hain (AND), isliye slicer + page filter ek saath lagane se result khaali aa sakta hai. Har filter ka intent likho aur 'clear all' affordance do, warna user ko confusion hoti hai.

items.q: Percentage-of-total measure kahan galat ho jaata hai?
items.a: Jab context (filter) ke hisaab se denominator badalta hai — jaise 'share of selected region' vs 'share of all'. ALL/ALLSELECTED ka farq yahi hai; purpose ke hisaab se explicitly chuno.

items.q: Dashboard me metric ka variance (noise) kaise handle karte ho?
items.a: Significance thresholds (min sample size), confidence band ya control chart, aur 'low sample' warning. Chhoti sample par 100% dikhana misleading hota hai.

items.q: DirectQuery aur Import mode me choice kaise karte ho?
items.a: Import: fast interactivity, scheduled refresh, memory cost — analytics ke liye default. DirectQuery: real-time/very large data, par latency aur query folding constraints. Hybrid (aggregations) dono ka mixture deta hai.

items.q: Data model me dimension table me duplicate rows hone par kya hoga?
items.a: Relationship ambiguous ban jaata hai, filters unexpected propagate hote hain aur visuals wrong aggregate karte hain. Fix: duplicate detect + dedupe with surrogate key, aur uniqueness test.

items.q: Report performance slow hai — pehla diagnostic kya?
items.a: Performance Analyzer se top visuals + DAX query times nikalo, cardinality-heavy columns (high distinct count) dekho, aur model size (memory) check karo. Aksar ek visual ka bi-directional filter ya high-cardinality column culprit hota hai.

items.q: Null aur unknown dimensions ko kaise handle karte ho?
items.a: 'Unknown'/'Not specified' member dimension me explicitly rakho — warna fans out joins ya rows gayab ho jaate hain. Fact me null foreign key ko Unknown (id -1) me map karo.

items.q: Same metric ke do numbers (report vs source) — kaise reconcile karoge?
items.a: Query ko source par dobara chalाओ with exact filters (date range, status, grain), phir step-by-step ek filter hatao/add karo jab tak numbers match hon. Reconciled definition ko documentation me lock karo.

items.q: Dashboard ka grand total individual rows ke sum se match nahi karta (distinct count case). Diagnose.
items.a: Non-additive metric (distinct customers) hai — individual sums se total zyada aata hai kyunki same customer kai rows me aata hai. Fix: total ke liye distinct count se calculate karo aur column me 'non-additive' note do.

items.q: Sales report me ek din ka data double dikh raha hai. Root cause?
items.a: Fact table me duplicates (retry/double load) ya join ne rows multiply kiye (many-to-many). Fix: load idempotency (unique keys), load-date audit, aur ek test jo daily totals expected fixture se compare kare.

items.q: Filter lagane par measure blank ho jaata hai. Kaunse cases?
items.a: Missing relation (filter table connect nahi), bi-directional off (filter propagate nahi hui), ya inactive relationship active nahi hua. Model diagram me relationship ka direction aur cross-filtering check karo.

items.q: Currency conversion report me total galat aata hai. Fix approach?
items.a: Currency rate ek dimension/table me date-based rakho aur conversion ko measure me lagao (SUM(amount * rate)), aggregate karne ke baad convert nahi. Rate grain (daily/monthly) document karo; missing rates ko 1 na maano.
items.x: Row level par convert, then aggregate.

items.q: Report me last month ke numbers 0 dikh rahe hain jabki data aaya hai. Pehla check?
items.a: Date classification/date range (date table refresh), timezone boundary, aur incremental refresh window. Aksar date dimension purane range par hi rehta hai.

items.q: Refresh 4 ghante le raha hai. Optimize kaise karoge?
items.a: Incremental refresh (sirf naya window), unnecessary columns/tables hatao, query folding verify karo, aur heavy transformations source (SQL/warehouse) par shift karo. Partition strategy se refresh window chhota karo.

items.q: Visual me top-5 dikha rahe hain par kaek product gayab hai jo fact table me hai. Wajah?
items.a: Visual-level filter ya top-N ka tie-breaking (ek hi value par kai products) ki wajah se. Fix: deterministic sort key (value + id) aur tie cases ke liye 'Others'.

items.q: DIVIDE se divide-by-zero se bacha, par output 0 aur blank ka farq confusion kar raha hai. Kya karo?
items.a: Intent decide karo: 'no data' ko blank rakho (visual me achha dikhta hai) aur galat 0 se bachao; display me custom format string se '-' dikhao aur tooltip me explanation.

items.q: Report ka 'as of' date aur source system ka date alag hai. Kaunsi galti?
items.a: Timezone (UTC vs local) ya refresh lag. Fix: sab UTC me store karo, display timezone explicit karo, aur refresh timestamp report header me dikhao.

items.q: Measure ka performance bahut slow hai (10s+). Typical culprits?
items.a: Row-level iteration (SUMX over high-cardinality table), bi-directional relationships, nested iterators, aur FILTER(table) instead of KEEPFILTERS/boolean filter. Optimize: aggregate first, filter columns not tables, aur measure ko decompose karke profile karo.

items.q: Slicer me ek value select karne par total same rehta hai. Bug?
items.a: Measure me ALL() use hua hai jo slicer ko ignore karta hai (ya context transition missing). Fix: ALLSELECTED use karo (slicer respect) aur measure ka intent document karo.

items.q: Numbers me 0.5% ka farq do reports me hai (rounding). Kaise fix karoge?
items.a: Rounding ka point decide karo (aggregate ke baad round, pehle nahi) aur decimal places consistent rakho. Ek hi 'rounded metric' layer banao aur baki reports wahi use karein.
items.x: Round karne ki jagah matter karti hai.

items.q: Text column par sort se months alphabetical ho jaate hain (April, August, …). Fix?
items.a: Month ko numeric sort column (month_number) ya date dimension ke saath rakho — display text, sort numeric. Ye classic date modelling mistake hai.

items.q: Report ka filter context test kaise karoge (manual clicking se better)?
items.a: Golden query tests: same filters ke saath expected numbers assert karo (DAX/Power BI REST API ya warehouse query se), aur model change par CI me chalao.

items.q: Null customer names report me blank dikhate hain. Fix?
items.a: Dimension me 'Unknown' member me map karo aur report me '(unknown)' label dikhao; saath me null rate metric rakho taaki data quality monitor ho.

items.q: BI me role-level security test karna hai — kya karo?
items.a: RLS roles ko test users ke saath impersonate karke verify karo, aur automated test rakho jo restricted region ka data sirf allowed user ke liye assert kare. RLS ko security boundary maano, UI filter nahi.

items.q: Star schema me slowly changing dimension type 2 ke baad reports double count kar rahe hain. Fix?
items.a: Fact ko correct version se join karna chahiye (event date between valid_from/valid_to) aur reports me current-attribute filtering ke liye separate 'current' flag/role dimension rakho. Warna ek customer kai rows me ginega.

items.q: Dashboard slow first load ke baad fast ho jaata hai. Kya ho raha hai?
items.a: Caching (visual cache/query cache) warm ho raha hai. Samjho ki first-load latency users ke liye important hai — aggregation tables, model size kam karo, aur often-used visuals ko pre-aggregate karo.

items.q: Excel/PBI me same pivot numbers match nahi kar rahe (grand total case). Pehla step?
items.a: Grain aur filters compare karo: rows ka grain (order vs order-line), status filter, aur date field (created vs paid). Phir ek QA query dono me chala kar farq isolate karo.

items.q: Incremental data me late-arriving rows purane days me aa rahe hain. Design fix?
items.a: Rolling window refresh (last N days har refresh me) + fact load idempotency (upsert by key), aur 'as of' reporting ke liye snapshot table. Late data ko accept karo, sirf duplicate se bacho.

items.q: Real-world: ML model ko production me deploy karna hai — end-to-end plan batao.
items.a: Artifact (model + preprocessor + version) → container/registry → CI (tests + eval thresholds) → deploy service with /health + /predict → monitoring (latency, drift, errors) → rollback plan + retraining job. Har step ka owner aur rollback path likho.

items.q: Real-world: Python service ka Docker image 2GB hai. Kaise kam karoge?
items.a: Multi-stage build (build deps alag stage), slim/base image, .dockerignore, layer caching (requirements pehle), aur non-essential tools hata do. 2GB se ~200MB possible.

items.q: Real-world: CI pipeline faster karna hai (15 min se kam).
items.a: Dependency caching, test parallelization, incremental builds, aur heavy jobs (model eval) nightly par move. CI me sirf fast deterministic checks rakho.

items.q: Real-world: container ko non-root aur secure kaise banao ge?
items.a: Non-root USER, read-only root filesystem jahan possible, minimal capabilities, no secrets in image (env/secret manager), pinned base image digest, aur vulnerability scan CI me.

items.q: Real-world: Git workflow for a small ML team banao.
items.a: Trunk-based with short-lived branches + PR review, protected main, conventional commits, aur model/data artifacts registry me (git me nahi). Tags/releases se deployments trace karo.

items.q: Real-world: production bug fix karna hai jaldi — process kya hoga?
items.a: Hotfix branch from production tag → minimal fix + test → CI → deploy with flag if possible → post-deploy verification → main me merge back. Incident log maintain karo.

items.q: Real-world: EC2 par app deploy karna hai (simple) — steps?
items.a: AMI/instance setup, security group minimum ports, SSH key/SSM access, systemd or container runtime, env config via secrets store, aur CloudWatch logs/alarms. Load balancer + autoscaling next step.

items.q: Real-world: S3 me model artifacts aur data rakhne hain — structure banao.
items.a: Prefix by purpose/environment/version (models/prod/v3/…), lifecycle policies (old versions to Glacier/delete), encryption on, versioning on, aur access via IAM roles (pre-signed URLs for temp access).

items.q: Real-world: IAM least privilege policy kaise likhoge?
items.a: Actions ko specific list karo (s3:GetObject, not s3:*), resources ARN-level restrict karo, conditions (source VPC/role) lagao, aur regularly access analyzer se unused permissions hatao.

items.q: Real-world: secrets production me kaise manage karoge?
items.a: AWS Secrets Manager/SSM Parameter Store (ya Vault), runtime par fetch with IAM role, rotation enabled, aur code/config me sirf references. .env sirf local dev ke liye.

items.q: Real-world: VPC me app aur DB kaise rakho ge?
items.a: Public subnet me load balancer/app (ya private + NAT), DB private subnet me (no public IP), security groups se sirf app→DB allow karo, aur flow logs on. Bastion/SSM se access.

items.q: Real-world: autoscaling group me app deploy karte waqt downtime zero kaise?
items.a: Rolling/blue-green deployment (new instances healthy hone par old terminate), ALB health checks, graceful shutdown (drain), aur immutable AMI/container tags. Saath me rollback AMI ready.

items.q: Real-world: monitoring aur alerting ka plan banao.
items.a: Golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation) + business metric; alerts sirf actionable thresholds par (burn rate/SLO), aur runbook link har alert me. Dashboard + on-call rotation.

items.q: Real-world: cost optimize karna hai AWS bill 30% — approach?
items.a: Bill ko service/tag-wise break karo, top 3 spenders identify karo (idle instances, over-provisioned RDS, data transfer/egress), right-sizing + reserved/savings plans + S3 lifecycle. Har change ka impact measure karo.

items.q: Real-world: backup aur disaster recovery plan kya hoga?
items.a: RPO/RTO define karo, automated snapshots + cross-region copy, restore drills (sirf backup hona kaafi nahi), aur runbook with exact restore steps + verification queries.

items.q: Real-world: data pipeline ka orchestration kaise karoge?
items.a: Airflow/Prefect jaise orchestrator me DAG (extract → validate → transform → publish), retries aur alerting, idempotent tasks with partition keys, aur lineage tracking. Manual cron se scale nahi hota.

items.q: Real-world: model retraining ko automate karna hai — design?
items.a: Scheduled/triggered job (drift ya data availability), same training pipeline with pinned data snapshot, eval gates (metric threshold pass hone par hi promote), registry + versioning, aur automatic rollback if canary degrades.

items.q: Real-world: A/B test infrastructure ke liye minimum kya chahiye?
items.a: Deterministic assignment (hash of user id → bucket), assignment logging + exposure events, metric definitions, significance calculation (sample size decide pehle), aur guardrail metrics.

items.q: Real-world: feature flag system ka minimal design?
items.a: Flag store (key, default, rules, rollout %), SDK with local cache + periodic refresh, evaluation logs, aur kill switch. Rollout % user-id hash par stabile rakho (user ko flip na kare).

items.q: Real-world: on-call handoff aur incident process banao.
items.a: Severity levels, ack SLA, communication channel + status page, incident commander role, aur blameless postmortem with action items + owners. Runbooks incidents se update hote rahein.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhara deployment architecture explain karo (2 minute me).'
items.a: Client → CDN/ALB → container service (N replicas, health checks) → managed DB (private subnet) + Redis; artifacts registry se deploy, CI me tests + eval gates, CloudWatch/OTel se observability, aur rollback AMI/tag ke saath.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne CI me kya checks lagaye aur kyun?'
items.a: Lint + typecheck, unit/integration tests, Docker build, model eval threshold (quality gate), aur security scan (deps + image). Fast checks PR par, heavy eval nightly — isse feedback loop fast rehta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Production me tumhara rollback process kya hai?'
items.a: Immutable versioned artifacts (image tag/AMI) se previous version par switch (ALB/ECS service update), DB migrations backward-compatible (expand-contract), aur rollback drill kiya hua. Target: <5 min.

items.q: Project defense: 'Secrets kabhi leak nahi honge — tumhara proof kya hai?'
items.a: Pre-commit + CI secret scanning (gitleaks type), secrets sirf Secrets Manager me with rotation, runtime fetch via IAM role, logs me redaction test, aur .env.example placeholders. Ek galti pakdi gayi thi — scan ne roka.

items.q: Project defense: 'Container image size aur startup time ka kya number hai?'
items.a: Image ~210MB (multi-stage, slim base), cold start ~1.8s, warm ~300ms. Isliye autoscaling me over-provision (buffer instances) rakha, aur health check grace period 10s. Measure kiye hue numbers hain.

items.q: Project defense: 'Database migration strategy kya hai (zero downtime)?'
items.a: Expand-contract: naya column/table add (nullable) → code dono versions handle kare → backfill batch job → constraint add → purana column drop alag release. Migrations versioned aur listed in CI.

items.q: Project defense: 'Cloud cost per month kya hai aur optimisation ka next step?'
items.a: Current: compute $X, DB $Y, storage/egress $Z (tag-wise breakdown). Next step: idle dev environments ka auto-shutdown + DB right-sizing; impact estimate 15-20% with measurement plan.

items.q: Project defense: 'Monitoring aur alerting me tumne kaunse false alarms hataye?'
items.a: CPU-based alerts hata kar SLO burn rate aur error-rate alerts rakhe; saturation counters sirf dashboard par. Alert fatigue ka metric: page volume per week — 30 se 4 pe aaya.

items.q: Project defense: 'Agar ek region down ho jaaye to tumhara system kya karega?'
items.a: Honest answer: single-region abhi SPOF hai; mitigation: multi-AZ (on hai), automated backups cross-region, aur documented DR plan with RTO 4h/RPO 1h. Full active-active next phase with read replicas + DNS failover.

items.q: Project defense: 'Load testing ke results kya the?'
items.a: Ramp test: 200 rps par p95 180ms, 600 rps par p95 900ms aur DB pool saturation — bottleneck DB connections tha, isliye pool tuning + read replica. Numbers aur bottleneck dono batao.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhara logging aur PII redaction kaise test hota hai?'
items.a: Log formatter unit test with PII fixture (email/phone) assert karta hai ki output me masked values hain, aur integration test logs capture karke scan karta hai. Isliye redaction silently toot nahi sakta.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer: tumne infrastructure as code use kiya?'
items.a: Haan — Terraform me VPC, ECS service, ALB, IAM roles aur secrets references; state remote me locked. Manual console changes discouraged; drift detect hota hai plan se.

items.q: Project defense: 'Deployment frequency aur lead time ke numbers batao.'
items.a: Deploy frequency ~5/week (main se deployable), lead time PR merge → prod ~1 day, change failure rate ~8%, MTTR ~20 min (rollback). DORA metrics dashboard par live hain.

items.q: Project defense: 'Model ya app ka version pinning kaise karte ho?'
items.a: Image digest, model artifact version, dependency lockfile, aur config version — sab deployment manifest me ek jagah record hote hain, isliye 'kya chal raha hai' ka exact answer 1 command me milta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Least privilege ke saath developer access kaise manage karte ho?'
items.a: SSM Session Manager / bastion via IAM role (SSH keys nahi), prod access temporary with approval, read-only by default, aur access logs. Break-glass procedure documented.

items.q: Project defense: 'Ek deployment fail hua — tumhara response kya tha?'
items.a: CI ne eval gate fail kiya (quality threshold), isliye deploy ruk gaya — merge nahi hua. Root cause: preprocessing version mismatch. Lesson: eval gate ko deploy path me rakhna (post-merge nahi) yahi value hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare stack me sabse weak link kya hai?'
items.a: Single-region deployment aur ek shared Postgres instance. Mitigation plan: multi-AZ (already), read replica for reports, aur next quarter cross-region backups + failover test. Honest naming + plan.

items.q: Project defense: 'Testing strategy production-grade kaise hai?'
items.a: Unit (pure logic), integration (API + test DB via containers), contract (OpenAPI schema), smoke (post-deploy), aur load test nightly. Coverage % ke bajaye critical paths par focus.

items.q: Project defense: 'Docker me data persistence aur state kaise handle kiya?'
items.a: Containers stateless (state DB/S3/Redis me), volumes sirf local dev ke liye, aur ephemeral filesystem assume kiya. Isliye restart/scale par data loss nahi hota.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer poochta hai tumhara runbook kaunsa incident cover karta hai.'
items.a: Runbooks: DB connection pool exhaustion, upstream API down (breaker open), disk full, deploy rollback, aur secret rotation. Har runbook me symptoms, diagnosis commands aur fix steps.

items.q: Checkpoint: Docker ke teen core concepts likho.
items.a: Image (immutable template, layers), container (running instance), aur registry (images ka store) — plus volume/network.

items.q: Checkpoint: multi-stage build ka fayda ek line me likho.
items.a: Build dependencies final image me nahi jaate, isliye image chhoti (aur attack surface kam) hoti hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: CI pipeline ke chaar stages likho.
items.a: Lint/typecheck → tests (unit/integration) → build artifact (image) → quality/security gates (eval threshold, scan) → deploy.

items.q: Checkpoint: 12-factor ke paanch factors likho.
items.a: Config in env, stateless processes, logs as event streams, declarative setup (build/release/run split), aur dev-prod parity.

items.q: Checkpoint: Git branching ke teen rules likho jo production safe rakhte hain.
items.a: Protected main (PR + review), short-lived branches from main, aur tags/releases se deploy traceability.

items.q: Checkpoint: secrets management ke chaar rule likho.
items.a: Secrets repo me nahi, managed store se runtime fetch, rotation enabled, aur logs/errors me redaction — plus least-privilege access.

items.q: Checkpoint: S3 bucket ke teen essential settings likho.
items.a: Encryption on, versioning on, aur public access blocked — plus lifecycle policies for old versions.

items.q: Checkpoint: IAM policy me teen cheezein restrict karo.
items.a: Actions (specific), Resources (ARN-level), aur Conditions (VPC/source/tag) — wildcard se bacho.

items.q: Checkpoint: containers me state kahan rakho?
items.a: Bahar: managed DB (transactional), object storage (files), cache/queue (Redis). Container filesystem ko ephemeral maano.

items.q: Checkpoint: observability ke chaar golden signals likho.
items.a: Latency, traffic, errors, aur saturation — plus business-level metric ek.

items.q: Checkpoint: RPO aur RTO ka matlab likho.
items.a: RPO = kitna data lose ho sakta hai (backup frequency se), RTO = kitni jaldi recover karna hai (restore speed se). Dono business se decide hote hain.

items.q: Checkpoint: blue-green vs rolling deployment ka farq?
items.a: Blue-green: poori nayi environment, instant switch + fast rollback (double infra cost). Rolling: instances ek-ek replace (gradual, kam resource, rollback slow).

items.q: Checkpoint: load test se kya seekhna hai (teen outputs)?
items.a: Knee point (kahan latency explode hoti hai), bottleneck (DB pool/CPU/network), aur capacity headroom + autoscaling trigger thresholds.

items.q: Checkpoint: alert design ke teen rule likho.
items.a: Actionable ho (runbook link), symptom-based ho (user impact), aur burn-rate/SLO based ho — noise alerts hatao.

items.q: Checkpoint: Dockerfile ke best practices chaar likho.
items.a: Pin base image version, requirements pehle copy karo (layer cache), non-root USER, aur .dockerignore.

items.q: Checkpoint: deployment rollback plan ke chaar element likho.
items.a: Immutable versioned artifact, previous version available, DB changes backward-compatible, aur documented + drilled rollback steps.

items.q: Checkpoint: cost optimization ke chaar lever likho.
items.a: Right-sizing, autoscaling/schedules (dev off-hours), reserved/savings plans, aur storage lifecycle + egress control.

items.q: Checkpoint: health check ke do types likho.
items.a: Liveness (process zinda — restart trigger) aur readiness (dependencies ready — traffic start).

items.q: Checkpoint: CI me model quality gate kaise lagate ho?
items.a: Frozen eval set par metric threshold (jaise F1 >= 0.85) aur regression guard (baseline se >1% gira to fail) — job fail hone par deploy nahi hota.

items.q: Checkpoint: incident response ke chaar step likho.
items.a: Detect (alert/report) → mitigate (rollback/flag off) → communicate (status page/stakeholders) → postmortem with action items.
